I'll fill in here. It's a concept marxists love to throw around called the "labour theory of value."

The idea is that value is a fixed resource which is created through labour, so your pile of metal might be pretty useless, but the car I turn it into is valuable. They then extrapolate from this point that business owners are unfairly exploiting workers by paying them wages, because they take the value the worker made and only give some of it back.

This completely nonsense argument (like most marxist ideas) ignores reality in two ways:

  • Value isn't a fixed resource, it's a subjective concept which varies from person to person. When a worker sells his labour he does so because he values the labour less than his wage packet, whereas his employer values the labour more than the money they pay for it.

  • The employee takes no risk whatsoever, they get paid no matter what. The employer risks their resources, hence the reward. Most businesses fail and the employer gets nothing. Which, if marxists were consistant, would mean that the employee exploited the employer.
